note.text: Deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level; disinflation is a reduction in the inflation rate. Prices can keep rising during disinflation when the rate remains positive. A single discounted item is not enough to establish general deflation. Persistent deflation can increase the real burden of a fixed nominal debt and may accompany weak spending and employment, though effects depend on the cause and wider conditions. A productivity-led relative price fall differs from a broad, prolonged demand contraction.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish a falling price level from a slowing rise and explain a possible consequence. Builds on: inflation rates, purchasing power and nominal debt. Leads to: banking and the monetary-policy role.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: Original comparison: an inflation rate slows from {8}% to {3}% while remaining positive, so the general price level still rises. A comparable broad index falling from {100} to {96} instead records a {100*(96-100)/100}% movement. The first is disinflation; a sustained general decline is deflation.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Look at the price level as well as the rate of change. Ask whether the measure is broad and the decline sustained. Do not turn a higher purchasing power of fixed cash into a guarantee that every household is better off when income or employment may also change.

example: deflation: a sustained fall in the general price level.

conditional welfare effect: Income, debt and employment outcomes also matter.

pick.q: Inflation slows from {8}% to {3}% and remains positive. Which description fits?
w: Deflation with prices falling.
An unchanged price level.
A guarantee of rising real wages.
e: Both stated rates are positive.
The later positive rate still raises prices.
No wage information is supplied.
pick.y: Slower increases are not decreases.

pick.q: A general price level falls persistently. Which description fits?
w: Positive inflation by definition.
Only a reduction in a still-positive rate.
A guaranteed improvement for every debtor.
e: The direction is downward.
The price level itself falls.
Fixed nominal debts can become heavier in real terms.
pick.y: Use the level direction and persistence.

pick.q: A shop discounts one notebook. What can be concluded about general deflation?
w: General deflation is proved.
All wages must fall.
All other prices must be unchanged.
e: A single item is not the general measure.
No wage data are supplied.
Other prices are unknown.
pick.y: Keep the evidence’s scope.

pick.q: Why may fixed nominal debt become harder to bear during broad deflation?
pick.r: Its repayment can represent more purchasing value.
w: Its nominal amount must become zero.
The lender loses all claims by definition.
Every borrower’s income is guaranteed to rise.
e: The nominal amount is fixed in the case.
No such cancellation rule is supplied.
Income can move differently.
pick.y: The real burden can rise without a nominal increase.
